items.description: The prior-plans sweep must surface plan-v1.md for this task slug AND carry its rejected decision: routing a streaming format through reporting/table.py:render is rejected, because render materializes the whole row iterator to size fixed-width columns and so reintroduces the memory ceiling NDJSON exists to avoid. Surfacing the plan's existence without the rejection does not satisfy this item — the rejection is the only thing that stops the run from repeating it, and nothing in the tree states it.

reporting/formats/csv_format.py offered as the exemplar to mirror: it is the streaming-shaped format module (writes per row, no materialization), which is the pattern the new module copies. Accepting table_format.py instead is not a match — it is the counter-example the prior plan rejects.

The report must state that adding a format needs NO registry edit — cli.available_formats discovers modules by scanning reporting/formats/ with pkgutil.iter_modules, so the new module file is the whole registration. Either the codebase-map row, the package docstring, or the matching learning (dedup_key f1a2b3c4d5e6) establishes it. A report that lists cli.py as a file needing a new Choice entry contradicts this item and does not match it.

The learnings sweep must surface the render() memory diagnosis (dedup_key a2b3c4d5e6f1) — render holds the entire row set to compute column widths, observed as an OOM on the 1M-row nightly report. It is the store-side evidence for the same constraint the prior plan rejected on.
reporting/source.py surfaced as relevant context — fetch_rows returns a lazy generator, which is what makes flat memory achievable at all. Optional: the new format consumes it without editing it.

The reuse inventory must classify the NDJSON writer itself as NO-ANALOGUE — neither existing format serializes per-row JSON, and json.dumps is stdlib, not an in-repo helper. A report that claims an existing format can be reused as-is for NDJSON is wrong, not a match.
tests/test_formats.py named as likely-touched — it holds one test per format and the new format needs its own; it is also the only test file in the tree.
change_scope reported as `trivial` or `small`: one new module file plus one test, no registry, no cross-module coordination.
